title: Digital transformation is becoming an economy-wide social system whose trust, well-being, and distributional effects need new measurement
source_unit: OECD, The OECD Going Digital Measurement Roadmap 2026
geography: International statistical and policy systems measuring digital economies, societies, technologies, and cross-border data flows

denominator.unit: OECD roadmap actions for monitoring digital transformation and its impacts

action_set.value: the roadmap proposes ten actions spanning economic statistics, data valuation, trade, AI, ICT impacts, well-being, skills, trust, timely data collection, and data infrastructure

silo_boundary.value: digital technologies and data are embedded across the economy and society, making a siloed digital-economy measure inadequate

policy_need.value: statistical systems need flexible, comparable, and interdisciplinary measures of digital transformation

observations.method: OECD policy paper synthesizing measurement priorities across economic, social, technological, governance, and statistical domains.
observations.uncertainty: The roadmap identifies measurement needs and priorities; it does not provide a single estimate of digital transformation’s net effect or guarantee cross-country comparability.
observations.subgroup: Individuals, firms, workers, consumers, governments, statistical offices, regulators, researchers, and groups exposed to digital disruption or exclusion.
observations.counterinterpretation: Existing economic and social statistics remain useful; new indicators should complement rather than replace established measures and should avoid measuring novelty without policy relevance.

observations.period: 2026; platform work, free services, and digital value

unpriced_consumption.value: online services provided to consumers at zero monetary price can still generate value and involve implicit exchanges related to personal data

platform_work.value: common definitions and survey questions are needed to measure platform-mediated work and transactions

cross_border_data.value: cloud services, online platforms, and data flows challenge geographically fixed production and trade measures

observations.method: OECD economic-statistics and digital-transformation measurement framework covering households, firms, platforms, services, and data flows.
observations.uncertainty: The paper does not estimate the value of any specific platform, the number of platform workers, or the welfare effect of exchanging personal data for free services.
observations.subgroup: Platform workers, households, online consumers, small firms, data-dependent businesses, and people whose work or consumption is mediated by platforms.
observations.counterinterpretation: Free digital services can provide substantial convenience and access; measurement of implicit data exchange should not assume that users experience it as a loss or that all data has equal economic value.

observations.period: 2026; digital well-being, inclusion, and harm measurement

wellbeing_scope.value: digital technologies can affect health, aging, environmental resilience, and individual well-being through both opportunities and risks

priority_groups.value: children, young people, women and girls, and people with disabilities require more specific measures of digital engagement, technology-facilitated violence, and algorithmic risks

distributional_need.value: disaggregated data can reveal digital divides and groups most exposed to technological disruption

observations.method: OECD social-statistics and well-being measurement recommendations for digital engagement, harm, opportunity, and distribution.
observations.uncertainty: The roadmap calls for better measurement but does not establish causal effects of digital exposure, algorithmic systems, or online harms for every subgroup.
observations.subgroup: Children, young people, women and girls, people with disabilities, workers, consumers, and communities with unequal connectivity or digital skills.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital technologies can expand access, participation, care, education, and services; risk measurement should preserve the possibility of positive and context-dependent effects.

observations.period: 2026; trust, privacy, security, and information integrity online

trust_conditions.value: security, privacy, consumer protection, and confidence in digital environments are increasingly important as daily activity shifts online

information_risk.value: manipulated and misleading online content can reduce trust and requires measurement of provenance, dissemination, and policy responses

infrastructure_need.value: timely data infrastructures, alternative data, private-sector cooperation, and privacy-preserving methods are needed to monitor digital activity

observations.method: OECD digital-governance and official-statistics roadmap connecting trust, privacy, consumer protection, information integrity, and data infrastructure.
observations.uncertainty: Measurement of trust or online content circulation does not itself establish the source, intent, or political effect of every information event; privacy and sampling constraints remain material.
observations.subgroup: Internet users, consumers, firms, regulators, statistical offices, journalists, civil society, and people vulnerable to fraud, surveillance, or misinformation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Security interventions can create centralized control or suppress expression if poorly designed; transparency, targeted safeguards, and freedom of expression must remain part of the measurement and policy frame.

related_sources.claim: OECD Going Digital Integrated Policy Framework provides complementary digital-policy governance context.
OECD Consumer Finance Risk Monitor 2026 provides complementary consumer-risk and digital-finance context.

boundary: This record adds a measurement-and-governance route linking digital economic value, platform work, data flows, AI, well-being, digital divides, privacy, consumer protection, information integrity, trust, and statistical infrastructure. It is a policy roadmap, not respondent-level digital behavior data, a causal impact study, a platform audit, or proof of any specific online harm.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official OECD Going Digital Measurement Roadmap 2026 PDF and full-report pages were reviewed for the ten actions, digital value and platform measurement, well-being and distribution, trust, privacy, consumer protection, information integrity, and data infrastructure claims.
